description_full: Dole plc engages in sourcing, production, distribution, and marketing of fresh fruits and vegetables worldwide. It operates through three segments: Fresh Fruit; Diversified Fresh Produce - EMEA; and Diversified Fresh Produce - Americas and ROW. The company offers bananas, pineapples, and plantains; avocados, kiwis, apples, berries, and cherries; and imported and local fresh fruits and vegetables through retail, wholesale, e-commerce, and food service channels. It is also involved in the commercial cargo business. The company offers its products under the DOLE brand. It serves grocery stores, wholesalers, mass merchandisers, supercenters, foodservice operators, club stores, convenience stores, distributors, and smaller regional customers. Dole plc was incorporated in 2017 and is headquartered in Dublin, Ireland.

CEO compensation is 13× revenue per employee (reasonable relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags moderate compensation governance risk (5/10).
financial_summary: Dole plc is a small-cap consumer defensive business with a $1.3B market cap on $9.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -0% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.

Returns on capital run at 7% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 8% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $2M in free cash flow — roughly 0 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.40× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 3.4×.

Shareholder yield of 2.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 11% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
